intended_object: For a subgroup H of a group G and two right transversals T and S of H, this is the canonical bijection T ≃ S that sends t ∈ T to the unique s ∈ S with Hs = Ht. The docstring says so, and the module uses it to show that corestriction does not depend on the choice of transversal.
explanation:
The forward map `changeRep T S` sends t to `(S.2.equiv t).2`. This is the S-component of the decomposition G ≃ H × S applied to t, i.e. the representative in S of the right coset Ht. The inverse is the same construction with the roles of T and S swapped. The proofs check that these maps are inverse to each other: each sends a representative to one in the same right coset, and an element of a transversal is its own representative.

So the map equals `(hT.rightQuotientEquiv).symm.trans hS.rightQuotientEquiv`, the composite bijection through H\G. Mathlib has no single declaration for this transversal-to-transversal bijection, only the two pieces.

The construction works for any subgroup of any group, and that is the generality used. The surrounding lemmas about `changeRep` are proved with `omit [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]`, which they could only be if `changeRep` itself takes no topological assumptions. It is a correct formalization of a minor but well-defined canonical object.
